# JIT 403 + long-poll

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:jit-authorization` · **Epic:** — · **Tickets:** 5 (2S 3M)

When a per-user grant is missing, the worker answers with a structured authorization_required response instead of forwarding: a 403 JSON body for HTTP and a JSON-RPC tool error result for MCP. The worker creates a pending authorization at the CP, and clients can long-poll its status to know when to retry.

## How we build it

- Body: {error:"authorization_required", provider, scopes, authorize_url:"<cp>/portal/connect/<pending_id>", status_url:"<cp>/connect/<pending_id>/status", pending_id, message}; Content-Type application/json; Cache-Control no-store.
- MCP (detected by mcpRequestScan): HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC result {isError:true, content:[{type:"text", text:<message + url>}], structuredContent:<same object>} echoing the request id; SSE-negotiated requests get the same result as one SSE event; stdio wedge emits the same result line.
- Pending creation: worker calls CP POST /connect/pending {sub, agent, provider, scopes} with its worker credential; CP dedupes on (sub, agent, provider, scopes) for active pendings; if CP is unreachable the worker returns 503 with error authorization_unavailable, never forwards.
- Status: GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=60s (max 60s) returns {status: pending|granted|denied|expired}; callers authenticate with a Warden user token whose sub matches or a portal session; waiters use the same in-memory notify pattern as the policy ETag long-poll.
- Events: deny event with reason authorization_required, provider and user sub; request never forwarded.

## Done when

A request needing a missing grant gets the structured 403 (or MCP tool error) with working authorize and status URLs, nothing reaches upstream, and the status long-poll returns granted within a second of consent completing.

### 1/5 · W-P3-JIT-01

**Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Add POST /connect/pending in internal/oauthbroker mounted on the CP behind worker authentication. Validate provider and cap scopes against the agent's perUserSecrets; return an existing active pending for the same (sub, agent, provider, scopes) or create one with 15m expiry. Response {pending_id, authorize_url, status_url, expires_at}.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Two calls with the same tuple return the same pending_id
- [ ] An unauthenticated or user-token call returns 401
- [ ] Scopes outside the agent cap are dropped from the stored pending

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-02`](oauth-broker.md#25--w-p3-brkr-02) Add pending authorization and grant metadata stores

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-JIT-02`](jit-authorization.md#25--w-p3-jit-02) Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing; [`W-P3-JIT-04`](jit-authorization.md#45--w-p3-jit-04) Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP

### 2/5 · W-P3-JIT-02

**Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

Add a jitDeny stage in internal/proxy/http.go run when swapSecrets sets s.authRequired: call a new CP client method CreatePending (internal/worker provides it via a Proxy seam with a 3s timeout), write the 403 JSON body with writeJSONResponse, record a deny event (reason authorization_required, provider) and log the decision. CP failure returns 503 authorization_unavailable. Request body is never forwarded.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Fake upstream receives zero requests when the grant is missing
- [ ] Response body matches the documented JSON schema (golden test)
- [ ] CP down yields 503 with error authorization_unavailable

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-01`](jit-authorization.md#15--w-p3-jit-01) Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations; [`W-P3-PUS-04`](refresh-model.md#45--w-p3-pus-04) Swap per-user placeholders in the proxy using verified sub

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-JIT-03`](jit-authorization.md#35--w-p3-jit-03) Return JSON-RPC tool error for MCP calls missing a grant

### 3/5 · W-P3-JIT-03

**Return JSON-RPC tool error for MCP calls missing a grant**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

When s.wasMCP and the call is tools/call, answer with HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC result {isError:true, content, structuredContent} carrying the same fields and the original request id; for SSE-accepting clients send it as a single text/event-stream event. Add the same result builder to internal/mcp/stdio (next to blockError) for the stdio wedge. Non tools/call MCP methods get a JSON-RPC error -32001 with the same data.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An MCP tools/call missing a grant returns isError=true with structuredContent.error == authorization_required
- [ ] The response id matches the request id
- [ ] SSE clients receive one well-formed event

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-02`](jit-authorization.md#25--w-p3-jit-02) Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-JIT-05`](jit-authorization.md#55--w-p3-jit-05) Document the authorization_required contract

### 4/5 · W-P3-JIT-04

**Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

Add GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=Ns (cap 60s) returning {status, provider, expires_at}. Authenticate with a verified Warden user token (Dex or CP-issued) or portal session; sub must match the pending's sub, else 404. Waiters register on a per-id channel that CompletePending and ExpirePending close, mirroring the policy server's long-poll notify; return immediately if status is terminal.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A waiter returns granted within 1s of the callback completing
- [ ] wait above 60s is clamped and returns pending on timeout
- [ ] Another user's token gets 404

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-JIT-01`](jit-authorization.md#15--w-p3-jit-01) Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-JIT-05`](jit-authorization.md#55--w-p3-jit-05) Document the authorization_required contract
